key_insight: In controlled wake flows, nonlinear autoencoders compress better, but POD produces smoother latent dynamics that are easier to forecast reliably over longer horizons.
engineering_relevance: For real-time flow control, the most compact latent space is not always the best choice; forecast stability can matter more than maximum compression for MPC and learning-based controllers.
method: Compare POD with convolutional autoencoders and two variational autoencoders for spatial compression.
Train LSTM-based temporal predictors on latent coordinates for two 2D actuated wakes: a simplified truck wake and the fluidic pinball.
Assess short-term reconstruction quality and long-horizon forecast stability of the resulting ROMs.
evidence_signal: Across the two controlled wake datasets, CAEs gave sharper short-term reconstructions, but POD-based latent trajectories were smoother and yielded more reliable long-horizon predictions with fewer catastrophic failures.
watch_item: Higher compression from CAEs can introduce irregular, broadband latent dynamics that destabilize forecasts, so encoder choice should be tested against the intended prediction horizon and control objective.
paper_title: The balance between compactness and forecast accuracy of data-driven latent-space reduced-order models in controlled wake flows
